newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia needs HRK 1.4 bln to revive 16 state firms.
newsitem.headline: Croatia needs HRK 1.4 bln to revive 16 state firms.

text.p: Croatia said on Friday it would need 1.38 billion kuna (some $250 million) to revive 16 troubled state-owned firms it decided to overhaul late last year.
"The financial consolidation has to ensure that these companies don't come back asking to be rehabilitated again," Deputy Prime Minister Borislav Skegro told reporters.
The latest government step follows the rehabilitation of over 20 other enterprises in 1996 as well as five shipyards, said Nada Mamic, a government's economic adviser.

She said it should enable firms including metal, plastics and textile factories, repair docks and wood processors from all over Croatia, get back on their feet and revert to profitability with the help of new business programmes.
They are also to be prepared for privatisation.

Typically, these are debt-ridden companies with blocked accounts, shrunken production and a 20-30 percent surplus in workforce, estimated to total 10,500. Some of them owe the workers pay for a number of months.

As in previous overhauls, their consolidation will comprise writing off almost all debts to ailing banks and reprogramming with a two-three year grace period where money is owed to state institutions, Mamic said.
Part of the mounting debt to creditors is to be swapped for around 700 million kuna shares from the government's portfolio.

The government has also pledged considerable funds for redundance pay and other forms of support to some 2,600 workers who will lose their jobs in restructuring. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
